media_work.title: A Crime on the Bayou
media_work.publisher_or_network: Augusta Films, Get Lifted Film Company, Artemis Rising Foundation (Distributed by Shout! Studios)
media_work.focus_or_theme: Tells the story of Gary Duncan, a Black teenager arrested in 1966 in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana, for touching a white youth's arm while trying to de-escalate a confrontation. Chronicles his challenge against the segregated justice system, aided by young Jewish attorney Richard Sobol, leading to the landmark Supreme Court case *Duncan v. Louisiana*.
media_work.summaryNotes: The case established the right to a jury trial for serious offenses in state courts, incorporating the Sixth Amendment right via the Fourteenth Amendment.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Tells the story of Gary Duncan, a Black teenager arrested in 1966 in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana, for touching a white youth's arm while trying to de-escalate a confrontation. Chronicles his challenge against the segregated justice system, aided by young Jewish attorney Richard Sobol, leading to the landmark Supreme Court case *Duncan v. Louisiana*.
media_item.summary_notes: Documentary about Gary Duncan, a Black teenager arrested in 1966 for touching a white youth's arm. It chronicles his challenge against the segregated justice system, leading to the Supreme Court case *Duncan v. Louisiana*.
key_quotes_raw: Interviews with Gary Duncan and potentially Richard Sobol (or archival), detailing the events of the arrest
the atmosphere of hostility and racism in Plaquemines Parish under Leander Perez
the legal strategy challenging the denial of a jury trial
and the significance of the Supreme Court victory.
systemic_issues_raw: Deep-seated institutional racism in the Jim Crow South
weaponization of the legal system against Black citizens
denial of fundamental constitutional rights (right to jury trial)
courage required to challenge systemic injustice
importance of Supreme Court precedents in advancing civil rights.
policy_recommendations_raw: Highlights the importance of enforcing constitutional rights, particularly the right to a fair trial by jury
serves as a historical reminder of the fight against systemic racism in the legal system.

external_links_raw.description: Supreme Court opinion for *Duncan v. Louisiana*

featured_individuals.time_served: *Unclear if sentence was served before/during appeals.*
featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Charged with and initially convicted of simple battery.
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Gary Duncan was wrongfully prosecuted and initially convicted of simple battery. His fight led to the landmark Supreme Court ruling in *Duncan v. Louisiana*, guaranteeing the right to a jury trial in state courts for serious crimes. It is unclear if his sentence was served before or during appeals.
contributing_factors_raw: Pervasive systemic racism in the Jim Crow South
abuse of power by local white supremacist officials (Leander Perez)
denial of the constitutional right to a jury trial for an offense deemed "serious" based on potential punishment (up to 2 years).
organizations_involved_raw: Lawyers' Constitutional Defense Committee (Richard Sobol volunteered).
